items.title: Dick Griffin interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 12, 2024
items.q: So my friend, God rest his soul, Paul Woods got put in jail for drinking. You know? He got arrested, he was inebriated. So my mother, being her good soul, “You’ve got to get Paul out.” So my money that I had saved a whole year, I bailed Paul out

ctx.x: Wow. Wonderful. Let me move you up to summers in Chicago and if my sources are correct you’re walking down the street and you hear what turned out to be Sun Ra?

Yeah. That was interesting. So my whole career kind of started in 1959. In ’58 I graduated from high school, my good mother — I would save my money. I was very good at saving. I majored in business in high school. I learned a lot about money. Thank God I’ve been able to apply — to stay on the right end of money you know. And so I had saved a hundred dollars, I remember very clearly. ’58 was supposed to be the year that I would go to Chicago and when I went, if I had gone in ’58 it would have been the first time…

had been around a lot of the criminals and street people — I wouldn’t say criminals, a lot of people that were on the funny side of the law and knew how to hustle and all that stuff. So I was very aware to a certain extent of what the street was like. But she said, “Okay you’ve got to be in after 7 o’clock or dark. So I was walking in the street in Chicago and I heard live music and you know I was definitely into music, I played in clubs and all that stuff. So I walked in and there was Sun Ra, there was Marshall…
